benefits_h2: Picture Every Product on an AI Fashion Model

benefits.alt: An adult woman with short silver hair wears a plain heather-gray hoodie in a studio.
benefits.t: Launch New Collections Without the Studio
benefits.d: Getting the model, the photographer, and the stylist into one day slows every drop, and one late hour can hold the whole launch. Upload several product photos and see the outfit on a realistic virtual model right away. You skip the casting and the studio booking. Preview the set and refresh the listing in minutes so you can sell sooner.

benefits.alt: An adult man with short auburn hair wears a plain denim jacket on a sidewalk.
benefits.t: Keep Product Photos Consistent on Every Channel
benefits.d: Light and pose shift every time you book a new shoot, so the catalog stops looking like one brand. Tops, jewelry, eyewear, and the rest of the line can share one model and one setting. Shoppers then recognize the line on your site, in the marketplace, and in the lookbook. Save that model and reuse it on the next collection.

benefits.alt: An adult woman with a tight bun wears a plain cream knit top on a bright terrace.
benefits.t: Boost Conversions With Realistic Virtual Models
benefits.d: Shoppers look closer when they can picture the piece on a body. Show how it sits, how the fabric falls, and how the cut reads. Pair the worn photo with a flat lay, or with a hanger shot that has nobody in it. Pick models of different ages and body types, then download a sharp file for the page.

steps_h2: How to Make AI Fashion Model Photos in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: A flat photo, or a photo of someone already wearing the piece, is enough.

steps.d: Pick the product photo you want on a virtual model. A flat lay works, and so does a photo of someone wearing it.
Pick a model that fits the brand, then pick the pose and the background you want on the listing.
Choose a tall, wide, or square frame. In a few seconds the download shows your product on the model you picked.

faq.q: Can I use this for the store and the lookbook?
faq.a: Yes. Use matching model photos across product pages and lookbooks. Change the background and lighting to keep the collection consistent.

faq.q: What image sizes can I download?
faq.a: Choose tall, square, or wide photos for your store and ads. Available sizes include 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, and 3:4.

faq.q: How close is a virtual model to a studio photo?
faq.a: Virtual model photos can look like studio images with natural poses and light. Check fabric, fit, and small details against the real item before publishing.

faq.q: How does a virtual model photo get made for clothing?
faq.a: Upload a clear garment photo and choose a virtual model. The tool places your clothing on a lifelike person with natural lighting, without a studio shoot.

faq.q: What if a small print looks different?
faq.a: Check each finished photo against the garment before posting. If a print or seam looks wrong, change the image and make another version.

faq.q: Can I put my own products on a virtual model?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the clothing or accessory you sell and choose a virtual model to wear it. You can make catalog photos in minutes.

faq.q: Can I publish these photos on my store and in ads?
faq.a: Yes. Use watermark-free model photos on product pages and in paid ads. Keep a clear product photo alongside them when shoppers need to inspect details.

faq.q: Can I make virtual model photos through an API?
faq.a: Yes. You can send garment photos from your store software through the API. This helps create model photos for a large catalog.

faq.q: How can virtual models help my fashion shop?
faq.a: They put your clothing on lifelike models without a shoot. Make consistent photos for product pages, lookbooks, and ads in minutes.

faq.q: Can I create model photos for an entire collection?
faq.a: Yes. Create on-model photos for each item or color in your collection. One photo costs 24 credits, so you can plan the cost before starting.

steps.prompt: Show this gray hoodie on an adult man facing the camera on a tree-lined street. Keep the hood, the two drawstrings, the pocket, the seams, and the gray color. Show his face and the whole hoodie.
steps.sourceHint: Keep the complete hoodie, hood, drawstrings and pocket visible.

reasons.h2: Scale the Catalog With Virtual Models
reasons.lead: One saved model can cover the next color, the next channel, and the next drop.

items.t: Save the Model and Reuse It
items.d: The face and the pose that fit the line stay saved. The next piece starts from that model, so you are not casting again.

items.t: Jewelry and Eyewear on a Model
items.d: A thin chain or a pair of glasses reads more clearly on a person. Use the [jewelry](page:tpl-jewel) page for that tight frame, and keep the clasp in view.

items.t: One Look on the Site and the Marketplace
items.d: Publish the worn photo on your own page first. When that file also goes to an [Amazon](page:plat-amazon) listing, point the [Shopify](page:plat-shopify) collection at the same photo so the shop still looks like one brand.

items.t: Hold the Pose and the Light
items.d: Pick the pose and the setting once. The next color inherits both, so the catalog does not shift every time you add a shade.

trust.h2: What Sellers Notice After the Worn Photo
trust.lead: The change shows up in the listing, the photo bill, and how much of the catalog looks ready.

items.t: Shoppers Can Picture the Piece
items.d: A worn photo helps a shopper see the product on a body, which is what turns a glance into a closer look.

items.t: A Smaller Photography Bill
items.d: You skip model day rates, studio rental, and a round of retouching. Each worn photo is 24 credits, and that charge is shown before it runs.

items.t: More of the Catalog Can Sell
items.d: Hero pieces used to get the only shoot. The rest of the line can get a worn photo too, so more styles look ready to buy.

items.t: One Look the Buyer Recognizes
items.d: A buyer moving from one style to the next still feels they are in your shop. The saved setting and the same model do that.
